records.summary: De Nederlandsche Bank does not print the euro banknotes allocated to it; one of the three private printers it awarded framework agreements to in December 2023 is Oberthur Fiduciaire of France.
records.detail: Contract-award notice 65988-2024, published in the EU's official procurement journal (Tenders Electronic Daily) on 1 February 2024 by De Nederlandsche Bank N.V. of Amsterdam, records framework agreements under the title 'Supply of Euro Banknotes ES2 2025 -2028', with the award decision dated 21 December 2023 and three winners: Oberthur Fiduciaire SAS (France), Giesecke+Devrient Currency Technology GmbH (Germany) and Bundesdruckerei GmbH (Germany). The notice's own description states that 'the Contracting Authority and the other Participating NCBs may issue Orders amongst all Contractors for ES2 banknotes for the production year 2025 and 2026', so orders are spread across the three printers rather than given to one. The notice number, title, winners, winner countries and award date here were read from TED's public API (api.ted.europa.eu/v3/notices/search), because the TED web page is served behind an AWS WAF challenge that refuses automated clients; the same notice opens in a browser at the URL given. Checked again against the API on 17 November 2026: buyer 'De Nederlandsche Bank N.V.', title 'Supply of Euro Banknotes ES2 2025 -2028', notice type can-standard, winner names 'Oberthur Fiduciaire SAS', 'Giesecke+Devrient Currency Technology GmbH', 'Bundesdruckerei GmbH', award decision 21 December 2023. The API returns winner countries as a separate array in a different order from the names, so the country given for each firm here is the firm's own home country and not a position in that array.

records.summary: Giesecke+Devrient's currency arm in Germany is one of three printers De Nederlandsche Bank awarded framework agreements to for the euro banknotes allocated to the Dutch central bank for 2025 to 2028.

records.detail: The same De Nederlandsche Bank contract-award notice, 65988-2024 of 1 February 2024 in Tenders Electronic Daily, lists Bundesdruckerei GmbH (Germany) alongside Oberthur Fiduciaire SAS and Giesecke+Devrient Currency Technology GmbH as winners of the framework agreements 'Supply of Euro Banknotes ES2 2025 -2028', award decision dated 21 December 2023. Bundesdruckerei already appears on the map as a printer for the Deutsche Bundesbank, so the Dutch tie puts the same firm on a second central bank. Notice fields read from TED's public API, the TED web page being behind an AWS WAF challenge for automated clients; no winner city is given in the notice data, so the head-office city is left null.

records.quote: Supply of EURO 5 ES2 banknote paper
records.summary: The Bank of Greece buys the paper for the five-euro notes it is allocated from EuropaFi in France, which has won the Greek central bank's banknote-paper contract in three successive years.
records.detail: Contract-award notice 309272-2026, published in Tenders Electronic Daily on 6 May 2026 by the buyer named as 'BANK OF GREECE', is titled 'Supply of EURO 5 ES2 banknote paper' and gives the winner as EUROPAFI SAS of France with a tender value of EUR 892,921.20. Earlier award notices under the same title went to the same company on 5 August 2024 (469305-2024) and 9 September 2025 (588433-2025). This is the banknote-paper relation rather than the printer relation, filed because the Bank of Greece was not previously on the paper row; EuropaFi already appears on the map as the paper maker for the Banque de France. That the Bank of Greece buys ES2 banknote paper itself, together with the ECB's published allocation of five-euro production to GR, points to printing in its own works, but no source read in this round states who prints the notes, so no printer tie is filed. Notice fields read from TED's public API; the TED web pages return an AWS WAF challenge to automated clients and open normally in a browser.

blanks.note: NLD converted to three records above. leads_not_opened: The single document that could settle the most places: the tender documents behind De Nederlandsche Bank's framework agreements. Award notice 65988-2024 says orders may be issued by 'the Contracting Authority and the other Participating NCBs', so DNB ran a joint euro-banknote procurement for several NCBs without printing works of their own. The participating NCBs are not named in the structured notice data; the earlier contract notice 351379-2023 and the 'Selection Guidelines' it refers to would name them, and if they include EE, IE, CY, LU, MT, SI, SK and FI, the three printers filed for NLD would apply to those places too. Do not assume that: get the list.

ECB's production statistics page, https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/euro/production/html/index.en.html, carries the full table of 'NCBs commissioning production' by denomination for every year from 2002 to 2028. It settles which countries have an allocation but never who prints it. It is a good source for the allocation itself if the map ever wants that as a separate fact.

ECB press release of 22 October 2004, https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2004/html/pr041022.en.html, sets out the framework: a single Eurosystem tender procedure for euro banknote production, with the rule that 'NCBs with in-house printing works or those using public printing works may decide not to participate in the single Eurosystem tender procedure and will then continue to produce the euro banknotes allocated to them in those printing works'. That is the mechanism, not a record, so nothing was filed from it, but it explains the split: in-house printers keep their own production and the rest tender.

TED's web interface is behind an AWS WAF challenge (HTTP 202, empty body, header x-amzn-waf-action: challenge) for every automated client, while its public API at api.ted.europa.eu/v3/notices/search answers freely and carries buyer, winner, winner country, contract title, award decision date and tender value. Expert-query syntax that works: 'buyer-name ~ ("Central Bank of Malta")', 'FT ~ ("banknote printing")', 'classification-cpv IN (22430000)' (22430000 is the banknotes CPV; 22440000 is the broad stamps-and-cheque-forms class and is mostly noise), 'buyer-country IN (BEL IRL ...)', 'notice-type IN (can-standard veat)'. Passing an unsupported field name makes the API dump its whole 60,000-character field list, so use only fields seen to work.

Croatian notices 620533-2019, 128252-2020, 434495-2020 and 570899-2020 (Hrvatska narodna banka, CPV 22430000 'Banknotes') need their winner names, which are not in the API's structured fields for old-schema notices. The EU open data bulk XML packages of TED notices are the route.
Slovak award notice 43839-2019 (Narodna banka Slovenska, 'printing services', 29 January 2019) and the Irish notices 361312-2019 and 180183-2026 need their texts read for the same reason.

Bank of Greece printing works (IETA) at Holargos: bankofgreece.gr returned HTTP 503 from this network on both paths tried, so the bank's own page was never read. The Bank of Greece annual report, as distinct from the financial statements served via athexgroup.gr, is the other route.
note: Four records, all from primary EU documents: three printers for the Netherlands and the banknote-paper maker for Greece. The euro-area structure was tackled first as instructed, and it mostly resists the printer row. The ECB publishes the allocation but not the printing: its production statistics page lists, year by year, which NCBs commission which denominations, and its 2004 press release explains that NCBs with in-house or public printing works keep their own production while the others tender. Neither names a printer for a country that tenders. Small NCBs' own reports are no better: Banka Slovenije's 2024 annual report says it 'is involved in the printing of euro banknotes at Eurosystem level' and books EUR 1.5 million of banknote production expense without naming anyone. What does name printers is the EU procurement journal, and there the whole euro area yields exactly one banknote award with named winners, De Nederlandsche Bank's framework agreements of December 2023 to Oberthur Fiduciaire, Giesecke+Devrient and Bundesdruckerei. Belgium, Ireland and Slovakia have published banknote tenders but no award notice with a winner; Cyprus, Estonia, Finland, Lithuania, Latvia, Luxembourg, Malta and Slovenia have none at all. One finding worth carrying forward: the Dutch award says orders may be placed by 'the other Participating NCBs', so that procurement was joint, and the list of participants would likely convert several of the eight blanks at once. The Greek record is deliberately on the sibling paper relation, not the printer relation: EuropaFi has won the Bank of Greece's 'Supply of EURO 5 ES2 banknote paper' contract three years running, which with the ECB's allocation of five-euro production to GR points at the bank's own works doing the printing, but no source read says so and bankofgreece.gr returned 503 on both attempts. The ten non-euro places went largely untested, which is the cost of the instruction to spend the budget on the euro structure: Timor-Leste was attempted and failed on three fetches (two IMF PDFs that returned HTML errors, and BCTL pages whose text is script-loaded), and San Marino failed because eur-lex returns an empty body to curl and refuses WebFetch by robots.txt. Those are recorded as 'not reached' rather than as documented negatives, because an absence from the ECB's allocation table is not a statement that a place has no banknotes. Ecuador, El Salvador, Palestine, Montenegro, Moldova, Madagascar, Guinea and Zambia were not opened at all. Fetch count: about 24 calls, of which roughly half were TED API queries and three were wasted on hosts that refuse this network (bankofgreece.gr 503, eur-lex 0 bytes, imf.org PDF paths).
